Goal: Determine all three angles of triangle.

\(CM\) is the internal bisector of \(\angle C\); therefore, by the angle‑bisector theorem  

\[

\]

The length of an internal bisector is known:

\[
CM =\frac{2\;AC\cdot BC\;\cos(\beta/2)}{AC+BC}

\]

### 2.  Using the given condition

\[

\]

### 3.  Solving for \(\beta\)

Let \(c=\cos\beta\;(>0)\).  With \(\cos\frac{\beta}{2}= \sqrt{\dfrac{1+c}{2}}\) (positive because \(0<\beta<90^{\circ}\)), (6) becomes  

\[
4c\sqrt{\frac{1+c}{2}}=4c^{2}+2c-1 .
\]

Squaring and simplifying yields  

\[
(2c+1)(8c^{3}-6c+1)=0 .
\]

The factor \(2c+1=0\) gives \(c=-\tfrac12\) (\(\beta=120^{\circ}\)), which would make \(\alpha\) negative, so it is discarded.

Thus  

\[
8c^{3}-6c+1=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 4c^{3}-3c=-\frac12 .
\]

Recall the triple‑angle identity \( \cos 3\theta = 4\cos^{3}\theta-3\cos\theta\).  
Setting \(c=\cos\theta\) we obtain  

\[
\cos 3\theta = -\tfrac12 .
\]

Hence \(3\theta =120^{\circ}\) (the other solution \(240^{\circ}\) gives \(\theta>90^{\circ}\) and does not satisfy (6) after taking the square root).  
Therefore \(\theta=40^{\circ}\) and  

\[
\boxed{\beta = 40^{\circ}} .
\]

Finally from (1)

\[
\alpha = 180^{\circ} - 2\beta = 180^{\circ} - 80^{\circ}=100^{\circ}.
\]
